To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the random phase approximation (RPA) can be rigorously justified in the limit of large systems and is a good approximation for the Hartree dynamics of a local defect embedded into a perfect crystal.
we have derived a rigorous mathematical model for crystals in the random phase approximation, and proved the existence and uniqueness for this model.

we have derived a mathematical formulation of the RPA model, and we have shown that it is equivalent to a macroscopic Maxwell equation, which is the first step towards a rigorous justification of the RPA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rigorous mathematical analysis of the nonlinear dynamics of a quantum system, which is of fundamental importance in the study of the electronic structure of crystals.
the rigorous derivation of macroscopic Maxwell–Poisson equations from the microscopic Schrödinger equation, and with the study of the corresponding time-dependent Hartree model.
the mathematical analysis of a nonlinear model of the polarization in crystals, and with the rigorous derivation of the Maxwell–Gauss law from the microscopic model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nonlinear Hartree equation describes the time evolution of the microscopic polarization of a perfect crystal with a local defect, and that, by means of suitable homogenization arguments, the nonlinear Hartree evolution converges to the Maxwell–Gauss evolution of the macroscopic polarization of the perfect crystal.

the random phase approximation is a mathematically sound approximation of the Hartree dynamics for crystals, and that the macroscopic Maxwell equations are the first order approximation of this dynamics.
, for the first time, we have a rigorous mathematical formulation of the RPA for crystals, which is consistent with the physics literature, and which is also mathematically rigorous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we give the first rigorous mathematical proof of the validity of the Maxwell–Gauss equations in the random phase approximation model for crystals.
we have developed a rigorous framework to derive a macroscopic Maxwell–Lorenz equation from a nonlinear microscopic model, and proved the convergence of the nonlinear dynamics to the linear dynamics.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, contrary to what happens for the linear response theory, the nonlinear Hartree approximation does not lead to a macroscopic model that is formally identical to that derived within the framework of the density functional theory.
the random phase approximation can be rigorously justified in the framework of the Hartree model.

the nonlinear Hartree equation, which is a model of a single electron interacting with a self-consistent field in the presence of an external field, is the right framework to describe the time evolution of the polarization of a crystal in the random phase approximation.
